_meta.purpose: Search aliases for properties whose town is not the name people search. The feed stores the postal town — 'Snowmass Village', 'Teton Village' — while every guest, brochure and ski map calls the place Aspen or Jackson Hole. Without an alias a search for 'aspen' returns five of the six Aspen-area houses and silently drops Viceroy Snowmass.
appliedBy: lib/atlas/place-aliases.js (query layer: lib/atlas/hotels.js — Guide search, cards, API)
lib/atlas/adapters/hotel.ts + public/maps/hotel/index.html (the atlas's own q haystack)
_meta.editingRule: Never rewrite `city` in luxury-hotels.json to the umbrella name — the town is correct, and a feed re-import would drop the edit anyway. Add a rule here; every consumer reads this file at load.
_meta.matching: A hotel joins a rule when its city equals `city` (case/accent-insensitive) and, where given, its adminRegion and country match too. The aliases are appended to the search haystack only — they never change the displayed city, the country facet, or the map's own city grouping.
_meta.scope: Umbrella-resort names only: the alias must be a name the property itself markets under. 'Beaver Creek -> Vail' is deliberately absent — those are separate mountains, and folding them together would mislead a client reading the map.

rules.note: Snowmass is one of the four Aspen Snowmass mountains, 12 miles from Aspen town; Viceroy Snowmass is sold as an Aspen stay.
Teton Village is the base of Jackson Hole Mountain Resort — Four Seasons Resort Jackson Hole and Caldera House both sit there.
The town of Jackson is the valley's other address; guests search the valley name.
